articles.headline: Ravens WR Flowers will play after having positive Rio workout
articles.description: Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers will play Sunday against the Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro after having an encouraging workout before the game, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Zay Flowers will play Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys in Rio de Janeiro after having an encouraging workout before the game.

Flowers had been considered a game-time decision with a left hamstring injury, and the Ravens didn't sound as if they were counting on him against Dallas, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter earlier in the day. But Flowers tested his injured hamstring in a 20-minute workout before the game, according to ESPN's Todd Archer, which convinced the team to make him active.

This means quarterback Lamar Jackson will have his top target for the first time since the first half of the season opener. In his return, Flowers is expected to be limited to 20 to 30 snaps, according to the NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.

Flowers has become one of Baltimore's most valuable playmakers. With Flowers this season, the Ravens have scored four touchdowns on five drives. Without him, Baltimore has scored three touchdowns on 16 drives.

In Baltimore's season-opening, 43-21 win at Indianapolis, Flowers aggravated his hamstring injury late in the first half and didn't return. He had produced a career-high 150 yards receiving in the first half, which was the most receiving yards by a Ravens player in 11 years.

Flowers didn't play in last week's 24-17 loss to the New Orleans Saints. He didn't practice Wednesday and Thursday before being a limited participant in Friday's walkthrough in Brazil.

On Friday's injury report, Flowers was officially listed as questionable. He has missed four games in his four-year career.

Last month, the Ravens signed Flowers to a four-year, $140 million extension that made him the fourth-highest paid receiver with an average of $35 million per season.

articles.headline: Fantasy football Week 3 inactives: Caleb Williams out, Puka Nacua uncertain, Sam Darnold a go
articles.description: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
articles.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists. 

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 3 Buzz 

Week 3 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 3

Biggest concerns heading into Week 3

Players with early starts

ACTIVE

DJ Moore, WR, Bills (shoulder): Moore is active for Week 3. He has not missed a game since 2020. It should be noted that Moore was limited and wore a noncontact jersey twice during this past week, so while fantasy managers should plan to start him, he may be somewhat limited.

Keon Coleman, WR, Bills (ankle): Coleman also missed practice this week, but was able to log a limited session Friday and is active. However, that is more of a boost for Josh Allen and the Bills than it is fantasy managers.

Jalen Coker, WR, Panthers (ankle): After missing practice Thursday, Coker returned in a limited fashion Friday -- his second practice of the week. He is active for Week 3. He has seen nine targets in both games this season. In fact, his usage is very similar to Tetairoa McMillan, only Coker is seeing a higher number of efficient targets.

 Malik Nabers, WR, Giants (shoulder): Nabers suffered his injury during "Monday Night Football" but was able to return to the field. He did pop up on the practice report this week but was able to log in full practices and is active for Week 3. He is a more volatile fantasy option with Jameis Winston under center -- especially this week with bad weather.

In most weeks, Nabers should still be viewed as a fantasy WR2. However, given the conditions today, lower him to a WR3. I would rather go with DJ Moore, Jaylen Waddle, Ladd McConkey or Tee Higgins. Play Nabers over Emeka Egbuka, Terry McLaurin, DK Metcalf and Jameson Williams.

Michael Pittman Jr., WR, Steelers (foot): After missing Week 2, Pittman was able to log limited practices this week and is active for Week 3. Even so, Pittman is nothing more than a low-floor flex option due to the struggling Steelers passing attack. The list of streaming options mentioned above are all receivers I would rather play than Pittman.

Jadarian Price, RB, Seahawks (chest): Price was limited at practice to start the week but got in a full practice on Friday and is active for Week 3. The Seahawks face the Commanders, who have been "middle of the road" against RBs. However, game script should largely be on Seattle's side. As such, Price is an RB2 play who can be started over Travis Etienne Jr., Warren, Rhamondre Stevenson and any Broncos RB. Emanuel Wilson could still see touches after he turned 21 car

articles.headline: Commanders LB Leo Chenal injured making tackle, carted off
articles.description: Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal was carted off the field with a neck injury after making a tackle late in the second quarter against the Seahawks.
articles.headlineJa: コマンダースのLBレオ・チェナルがタックル時に負傷、カートで退場
articles.descriptionJa: コマンダースのラインバッカー、レオ・チェナルは、シーホークス戦の第2クォーター終盤にタックルを決めた際、首を負傷してカートでフィールドを後にした。
articles.body:
LANDOVER, Md. -- Washington Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal was carted off the field with a neck injury late in the second quarter.

Chenal filled the hole on a run with 6 minutes, 47 seconds left in the first half where he tackled Seattle Seahawks running back Emanuel Wilson by appearing to lead with his head.

The linebacker immediately went to the ground as medical personnel were quick to run to his side. Teammates surrounded Chenal as the crowd chanted "Leo! Leo!" He was taken off on a cart, raising his left hand as he approached the tunnel. The Commanders ruled him out shortly before halftime.

Chenal was starting in place of the injured Frankie Luvu, who was missing his second consecutive game with a groin injury. The Commanders were thin at the position because another inside linebacker, Jordan Magee, was placed on injured reserve after the opener with a hamstring injury.

Second-year linebacker Ale Kaho, who was elevated off the practice squad for this game, replaced Chenal in the lineup.

articles.headline: Dolphins RB De'Von Achane suffers knee injury vs. Chiefs
articles.description: Dolphins running back De'Von Achane suffered a knee injury in Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- Miami Dolphins running back De'Von Achane will not return to the team's game against the Kansas City Chiefs after suffering a knee injury on their opening drive.

Achane took his third rushing attempt of the game 11 yards around the left end but was tackled awkwardly by Chiefs safety Alohi Gilman. He was slow to leave the field after the tackle but was eventually escorted to the blue medical tent under his own power. The Pro Bowler ultimately left the tent after a few minutes and was taken to the locker room for additional testing.

He did not return to the sideline in the first half but was seen on the Dolphins' sideline after halftime without his shoulder pads or helmet on and then ruled out.

The 2023 third-round pick missed five games with a knee injury as a rookie but has otherwise been more durable than his 5-foot-9, 195-pound frame would suggest, especially considering his workload. He missed two combined games over the past two seasons, despite handling 586 total touches in 2024 and 2025.

He's coming off the best season of his career in 2025, during which he recorded 1,838 yards from scrimmage and 12 total touchdowns en route to his first Pro Bowl.

Achane's 2026 season has started slowly, with 159 scrimmage yards on 38 touches through two weeks. Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley joked this offseason that Achane could get 40 or more touches each week but the running back said he hasn't raised any issues about his workload this season.

"I've never been that type [to complain about touches]," Achane said this week. "Me and Haf already had a conversation. He always wants me to -- if I see something, come up to him and tell us something, but I've never been that type of player to go to somebody and tell them what to do or say, 'Oh, I need the ball more.' I mean, I've never been that type of player, so I'm not going to start now."

With running back Jaylen Wright inactive Sunday with a stinger, the Dolphins only activated two running backs this week -- Achane and second-year back Ollie Gordon II, who punched in his first touchdown of the season following Achane's injury.

articles.headline: Bears QB Bagent clears protocol; Keenum likely to start vs. Eagles
articles.description: The Bears' Tyson Bagent has cleared the concussion protocol, but Case Keenum is expected to start Monday night's game at QB against the Eagles.
articles.headlineJa: ベアーズQBバジェントがプロトコルをクリア、イーグルス戦はキーナムが先発濃厚
articles.descriptionJa: ベアーズのタイソン・バジェントは脳震盪プロトコルをクリアしたものの、マンデーナイトのイーグルス戦ではケース・キーナムがQBとして先発する見込みだ。
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent has cleared the NFL's concussion protocol and does not carry an injury designation into Monday night's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Bagent, however, is expected to serve as the backup to Case Keenum against the Eagles. Keenum, 38, was the only quarterback on Chicago's 53-man roster to practice each day leading into Week 3.

Bagent was back at practice Saturday where he was a full participant after missing the Bears' prior two sessions. The Bears say that the 26-year-old backup sustained a concussion on his second play in relief of Caleb Williams in Chicago's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. After Bagent threw a short pass to his left that fell incomplete, he was driven to the turf by Minnesota outside linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel.

Williams was officially ruled out Saturday and has a Grade 2 hamstring strain that is expected to sideline him for three to four weeks, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

articles.headline: Parma part ways with ex-Arsenal assistant Carlos Cuesta
articles.description: Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.
articles.headlineJa: パルマ、元アーセナル助監督のカルロス・クエスタ氏と契約解除
articles.descriptionJa: パルマはセリエA開幕5試合でわずか1勝にとどまり、日曜日にカルロス・クエスタ監督と解任・退任の道を歩むこととなった。
articles.body:
Parma parted ways with coach Carlos Cuesta on Sunday after winning only one of their opening five Serie A matches.

The club said Cuesta "has been relieved of his duty" and that "following an internal discussion between the club and coach, it was agreed that the conditions in order to continue this working relationship and the advancement of the sporting project, were not being met. Both parties came to a mutual agreement."

- Goals galore! Why Barça's start to season is best in Europe's top leagues for almost 100 years

- Udinese sign former Real Madrid defender Alaba

- Havertz back at Arsenal for injury treatment

A replacement was not immediately named.

Parma beat Genoa last weekend but only have four points.

Cuesta became the youngest manager in Europe's top five leagues, and the youngest Serie A manager in almost a century, when he was appointed by Parma in June 2025 at the age of 29. He had previously spent five years as assistant to Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta.

Having decided at a young age that his future lay in coaching rather than playing, Cuesta was given his first chance at Atlético Madrid with their underage teams and after four years there, went travelling Europe to study coaching methods.

It was during this period that Cuesta met Arteta, then part of Pep Guardiola's coaching staff at Manchester City, and after a two-year spell with Juventus' youth academy, Cuesta joined Arsenal in 2020.

He guided Parma to a 13th-place finish last season.

It's the third coaching change in Serie A this season after Paolo Vanoli replaced Fabio Grosso at Fiorentina and Raffaele Palladino replaced Domenico Tedesco at Bologna.

Parma's next match is at Serie A champions Inter Milan on Oct. 10 after the international break.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: LaLiga chief Javier Tebas criticises Man City's alleged rule breaches: 'Equal rules for all'
articles.description: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential.
articles.headlineJa: ラ・リーガのテバス会長、マンCのルール違反疑惑を批判：「すべての人に平等なルールを」
articles.descriptionJa: ラ・リーガのハビエル・テバス会長は、マンチェスター・シティのプレミアリーグに対する法的闘争が、なぜ「すべての人に平等なルール」が不可欠であるかを示していると語った。
articles.body:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential to protect football's integrity and sustainability.

ESPN reported on Friday that a source has confirmed City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

In a statement, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

The Athletic first reported Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges by an independent panel.

- Ogden: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

In 2020, Man City succeeded in overturning a two-year European competition ban from UEFA at the Court of Arbitration, after being found to have breached the governing body's Financial Fair Play (FFP) rule.

Tebas had previously spoken out against "so-called financial doping in European football".

In a lengthy post on X, Tebas reflected on those statements he had given during the Soccerex event, which had been held in Manchester during September 2017.

Tebas also called the CAS ruling a "deeply misguided decision" which was "extraordinarily damaging to the credibility of European football's economic control system" and again stressed the same rules must apply to all clubs.

"Economic sustainability is not bureaucracy. Financial control is not a whim," he said.

"And arguing that clubs should compete fundamentally with the resources they are able to generate doesn't mean being against any specific club either. It's about defending a model.

"A model in which sporting success doesn't depend on who has the most powerful financial backing behind them, but on who manages best, generates more resources, builds better teams, and respects the same rules as everyone else.

"Defending this position has cost me a lot of criticism and not a few headaches. But I still think exactly the same as I did in Manchester in 2017.

"There are principles worth defending, even if they come at a cost. And this one, for me, is one of them.

- Man City chairman on club's Premier League charges case: 'Nothing has changed'

"Now, almost nine years after those words at Soccerex, an independent Premier League commission has deemed 114 of the 115 financial breaches charged against Manchester City proven, according to the published reports.

"There's still a way to go. The sanction remains to be known, and the process isn't over. But what's happened once again shows why economic control, transparency, and equal rules for all are essential to protect the integrity and sustainability of football."

"We will keep defending those principles. Just like in 2017."

Information from PA contributed to this story.
